discovery: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene: prediction and discovery of flat-band correlated insulating and superconducting states (twistronics)

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic' angle near 1.1 degrees flattens the electronic bands, so that interactions dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero and co-workers built such devices by a controlled tear-and-stack method and found correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity. Later work saw the result reproduced in many laboratories around the world. Twist angle became a new and continuously tunable control knob for quantum matter. The work started a whole field: moire materials have since shown orbital magnetism, the quantum anomalous Hall effect and fractional Chern insulators at zero magnetic field. This is the kind of discovery I value most. It is a clean, quantitative prediction followed by a feat of nanoscale fabrication, and it was robustly reproduced. It changed what physicists believe can be engineered from a single atomic layer of carbon.
